decisive_items: Hypercellular marrow consisting of 80% plasma cells with atypical morphology and κ-light-chain restriction
CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
response.rationale: The clinical and laboratory picture is diagnostic of multiple myeloma: hypercalcemia, renal failure, lytic bone lesions, monoclonal IgG-κ protein, and marrow replacement by clonal plasma cells. The cryoglobulinemia and intravascular cryoglobulin thrombi are secondary complications of the underlying plasma cell dyscrasia rather than a primary cryoglobulinemic disorder.

rejected.why: Cryoglobulinemia is present but is best explained as a secondary manifestation of multiple myeloma; the marrow findings, lytic lesions, and monoclonal plasma cell infiltration establish the primary diagnosis.
